title: A run's base refresh is a no-op when -base defaults to HEAD
description:
Every reconcile round since epic-dha was restarted has logged:

    base_refreshed | origin has no branch HEAD: there is nothing to refresh epic/dha from

-base documents itself as 'what the integration branch is cut from (default "HEAD")'. HEAD is not a branch name on the remote, so the refresh resolves nothing and silently does nothing, every round, forever. The feed line says so, but it reads like a note rather than a failure.

The consequence is not cosmetic. The run reads the TRACKER from its integration branch. A tracker change made on main - blocking a tick, adding a blocker, closing something out of band - never reaches a running epic. I hit this directly on 2026-09-20: I blocked u9h on 37i, pushed to main, and the run dispatched u9h again 40 seconds later because epic/dha had never heard of the block. The fix was to fold main into epic/dha by hand and push that.

So an operator's only supported way to steer a live run - the tracker - is disconnected from it by a default value.

Fix options, in preference order:
1. -base defaults to the repository's default branch, not HEAD. A run cut from HEAD is almost never what anyone means.
2. If HEAD is genuinely meant to mean 'resolve the remote's HEAD', resolve it (git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD) rather than looking for a branch literally named HEAD.
3. Failing either, make an unresolvable base a REFUSAL at run start, not a per-round note. A refresh that can never work should stop the run once, loudly, instead of reassuring it 400 times.

Found by watching a live run.
acceptance_criteria: A run started without -base refreshes its integration branch from the repository's real default branch, proven by a test that changes the tracker on the default branch and shows the running epic observing it
